- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. - code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. - pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- playwright-skill: Complete browser automation with Playwright. Auto-detects dev servers, writes clean test scripts to /tmp. Test pages, fill forms, take screenshots, check responsive design, validate UX, test login flows, check links, automate any browser task. Use when user wants to test websites, automate browser interactions, validate web functionality, or perform any browser-based testing.
- audit-tier: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- contentful-register-component: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
- generate-changelog: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
- new-component: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
- onboarding: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
- pr-checklist: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
- project-init: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
- qa-generate: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
- scope-check: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.
- session-start: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.
- upstream-sync-review: Review the release notes / changelog for a new @salesforce/retail-react-app version before bumping. Lightweight policy — see .docs/upstreamPolicy.md.
- agent-sdk-dev:new-sdk-app: Create and setup a new Claude Agent SDK application
- claude-md-management:revise-claude-md: Update CLAUDE.md with learnings from this session
- code-review:code-review: Code review a pull request
- commit-commands:clean_gone: Cleans up all git branches marked as [gone] (branches that have been deleted on the remote but still exist locally), including removing associated worktrees.
- commit-commands:commit-push-pr: Commit, push, and open a PR
- commit-commands:commit: Create a git commit
- feature-dev:feature-dev: Guided feature development with codebase understanding and architecture focus
- plugin-dev:create-plugin: Guided end-to-end plugin creation workflow with component design, implementation, and validation
- pr-review-toolkit:review-pr: Comprehensive PR review using specialized agents
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- vercel:bootstrap: Bootstrap a repository with Vercel-linked resources by running preflight checks, provisioning integrations, verifying env keys, and then executing db/dev startup commands safely.
- vercel:deploy: Deploy the current project to Vercel. Pass "prod" or "production" as argument to deploy to production. Default is preview deployment.
- vercel:env: Manage Vercel environment variables. Commands include list, pull, add, remove, and diff. Use to sync environment variables between Vercel and your local development environment.
- vercel:marketplace: Discover and install Vercel Marketplace integrations. Use to find databases, CMS, auth providers, and other services available on the Vercel Marketplace.
- vercel:status: Show the status of the current Vercel project — recent deployments, linked project info, and environment overview.
- claude-code-setup:claude-automation-recommender: Analyze a codebase and recommend Claude Code automations (hooks, subagents, skills, plugins, MCP servers). Use when user asks for automation recommendations, wants to optimize their Claude Code setup, mentions improving Claude Code workflows, asks how to first set up Claude Code for a project, or wants to know what Claude Code features they should use.
- claude-md-management:claude-md-improver: Audit and improve CLAUDE.md files in repositories. Use when user asks to check, audit, update, improve, or fix CLAUDE.md files. Scans for all CLAUDE.md files, evaluates quality against templates, outputs quality report, then makes targeted updates. Also use when the user mentions "CLAUDE.md maintenance" or "project memory optimization".
- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Routes to a direction-specific reference doc; loads alongside `figma-use` for the code → design path.
- figma:figma-use: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.
- figma:figma-use-figjam: This skill helps agents use Figma's use_figma MCP tool in the FigJam context. Can be used alongside figma-use which has foundational context for using the use_figma tool.
- figma:figma-use-motion: Motion / animation context for the `use_figma` MCP tool — animating Figma nodes via manual keyframes, animation styles, easing, and timeline duration. Load alongside figma-use whenever a task involves adding, editing, or inspecting animation on a node.
- figma:figma-use-slides: This skill helps agents use Figma's use_figma MCP tool in the Slides context. Can be used alongside figma-use which has foundational context for using the use_figma tool.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- plugin-dev:agent-development: This skill should be used when the user asks to "create an agent", "add an agent", "write a subagent", "agent frontmatter", "when to use description", "agent examples", "agent tools", "agent colors", "autonomous agent", or needs guidance on agent structure, system prompts, triggering conditions, or agent development best practices for Claude Code plugins.
- plugin-dev:command-development: This skill should be used when the user asks to "create a slash command", "add a command", "write a custom command", "define command arguments", "use command frontmatter", "organize commands", "create command with file references", "interactive command", "use AskUserQuestion in command", or needs guidance on slash command structure, YAML frontmatter fields, dynamic arguments, bash execution in commands, user interaction patterns, or command development best practices for Claude Code.

Audited the SFCC Confluence space for existing documentation/support for two assigned spikes. Full page inventory in [[reference-confluence-sfcc-space]]. Key findings:

**SFCC-122 (MRT API Capabilities):** No single canonical doc exists — the spike is genuinely needed, not duplicative. Closest existing material is "TSD: Catalogue Sync — SCAPI Admin API Design (Alternative Pattern)" (315490342), which documents SCAPI Admin APIs for Product/Inventory as an alternative to the recommended WebDAV file-based import. Critical finding baked into that doc: **no SCAPI Admin API exists for writing pricebook/price data** — price sync must always go through file-based WebDAV import regardless of pattern chosen. That doc's own Open Items (rate limits, bulk-operation support, Anypoint MQ sequencing) are still unanswered. "Mulesoft API Spec - Hub" (305659907) is a completely empty stub. Dependencies tracker row T2 "SFCC MRT API Capabilities" has blank SME Owner/Status.

**SFCC-123 (Contentful Integration TSD):** Strong head start already exists. "Contentful CMS — Setup & Operations" (318472193) covers environment topology, alias/release workflow, token scoping, and locale config (9 locale codes across 8 storefronts) — largely answers the spike's environment/locale tasks. "TSD: Product — SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration" (292061208) §6 already states the handoff boundary: Contentful owns only editorial content (banners/collection pages/lookbook/rich PDP copy) via Delivery API; all product/price/inventory data stays in SFCC via AP21→MuleSoft, never Contentful. That same TSD's Open Item #3 ("Define Contentful content model and connector customisation scope | Frontend Dev | Open") is effectively the same deliverable as SFCC-123 — worth cross-linking. Still genuinely open: Sprint 1/2 required content types beyond the current `shoppableImage`/`CollectionHero`/`ImageText` set, and which specific Contentful fields/rendering logic SFCC needs to consume. Several Human Setup Checklist items on the ops page are incomplete (MRT env vars per tier not set, cache-purge webhook not configured, content-type-editing roles not restricted, CI CMA token not added as a GH secret) — worth flagging as blockers per the spike's own task list.

**Discrepancy found:** Both Confluence locale tables (Contentful ops page and the Product TSD's multi-locale table) agree on 9 unique locale codes for the 8 storefronts (en, en-GB, en-US, fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE). This conflicts with AGENTS.md/testing.md's "11 active locales" figure for the same 8 storefronts — a real inconsistency that should be resolved as part of SFCC-123's locale task, since it affects Contentful locale bootstrap scope. Not yet raised with the user.

**Why:** these two spikes were the user's active assigned work as of 2026-07-15; both link to the Dependencies tracker (310050860) rows T1/T2, which are Sprint 1 blockers for Squad A.

<result># Confluence Guardrails Audit — SFCC Space

All pages fetched successfully (read-only; no edits made). Findings below, organized per the 8 requested categories plus a 9th for additional discoveries from the search step.

---

## 1. Branching Guide (GitFlow) — page 304840733

**Approval counts per branch:**
- `feature/*` → `develop`: **1 approval** required ("develop is a shared integration point")
- `fix/*` → `develop`: same as feature (1 approval, via `qa.yml` unit tests)
- `hotfix/*` → `main` **and** `develop`: approvals not stated on this page (see CI/CD page: 2)
- `release/**`: created by squad leads/CI from a tagged `develop` state — developers do not create these directly
- `fix/release-{version}-*` → `release/**`: PR back into the release branch; squad leads separately apply the same fix to `develop` via a second PR
- Direct commits to a release branch: only for **no-logic changes** (copy corrections, version bumps, boolean flag toggles) — require **explicit squad lead approval**

**Release tagging process:** `scripts/tagRelease.sh v{version}` run from `main` after the release PR merges — creates both `v{version}` and `release/digital/v{version}` git tags. Sprint boundary tags (`sprint/{N}/{date}`) are created automatically by CI when `scripts/sprint.txt` is updated.

**Version format:** Pre-go-live `v0.{sprint}.0`; go-live `v1.0.0`; post-launch patches `v1.0.{patch}`; post-launch features `v1.{minor}.0`.

**Merge restrictions:** Claude Code is "physically blocked" from writing to `develop`/`main` via a branch-lock hook in `.claude/settings.json`. On `release/**`, Claude Code runs in supervised/read-only-skills mode; code logic fixes must go through a `fix/release-*` sub-branch.

---

## 2. PWA CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions) — page 305561601

**Trigger matrix (workflow → jobs):**
- Push to `develop` → `digital-sit.yml`: install → playwright-p0, lighthouse-ci, contract-tests, bundle-size → sit-gate → deploy-sit → tag-sit-deploy, tag-sprint
- PR → `release/**` → `digital-sit.yml`: install → four signal jobs → sit-gate (no deploy)
- PR → `develop` or `release/**` → `qa.yml`: unit-tests, storybook-test (every PR) → e2e-browserstack (release/** only)
- PR opened (any branch) → `protected-file-guard.yml`: tier-1-guard, tier-2-guard
- Weekly cron (Mon 1am UTC) → `weekly-agents.yml`: quality-sweep, contentful-drift-audit, changelog-reminder
- Weekly cron (Mon 0:00 UTC) → `upstream-release-watch.yml`: check-for-new-release

**Branch protection — required approvals:**
- `develop`: **2 approvals** (one owning squad, one cross-squad), required status check `unit-tests`, branches must be up to date, no bypass
- `main`: **2 approvals** (both squad leads), same up-to-date/no-bypass rules; hotfix PRs into `main` still require 2 approvals
- `release/**`: required check = `Digital SIT Gate` composite job

**Digital SIT Gate thresholds (also gates `release/**` merges):**
| Signal | Tool | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| Playwright P0 | Playwright | 100% pass, all storefront configs |
| Lighthouse CI | LHCI | Perf ≥80, A11y ≥90, Best Practices ≥90; >5pt drop = blocked |
| MuleSoft contract tests | Pact/OpenAPI | Any schema breach = blocked (pending spec source) |
| Bundle size | bundlewatch | main.js <180kB, vendor.js <250kB, main.css <50kB |

**STAGE convergence gate:** manual, not a GitHub status check — checklist: Digital SIT Gate green + NewStore SIT complete + Integration Lead and both squad leads signed off.

**Commit message enforcement:** Layer 1 = local `commit-msg` Husky hook (types: feat/fix/docs/style/refactor/perf/test/build/ci/chore/upstream-sync). Layer 2 = CodeRabbit PR review (`coderabbit.yaml`).

**CI Secrets (names only):** `LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL`, `LHCI_TOKEN`, `LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT`, `MRT_USER`, `MRT_API_KEY`, `BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME`, `BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY`, `RETAIL_APP_HOME_SIT`, `PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL`, `PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD`, `E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER`.

---

## 3. SIT Quality Gates — page 304840754

- Four automated checks gate promotion to `release/**` — enforced by GitHub branch protection; cannot merge without green `Digital SIT Gate`.
- **Thresholds** (same as above): Playwright P0 100% pass; Lighthouse Perf ≥80/A11y ≥90/Best Practices ≥90 (>5pt drop blocks); bundle main.js<180kB/vendor.js<250kB/main.css<50kB; contract tests = any breach blocks.

input.content: # Zimmermann PWA Kit — Software Engineering Harnesses & Guardrails _Compiled from a full sweep of the `zimmermann-pwa` repo and the Confluence `SFCC` space, 2026-07-16._ _Scope: mechanisms that automatically enforce quality, security, or process — not general conventions that rely on a human/Claude reading a doc._ --- ## 1. Branch & Merge Guardrails | Branch | From | Merges to | Required approvals | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---| | `feature/*`, `fix/*` | `develop` | `develop` | **1** (unit-tests required check) | Primary working branches | | `release/**` | `develop` | `main` + `develop` | Required check = **Digital SIT Gate** (composite) | Created by squad leads/CI from a tagged `develop` state, not by developers directly | | `fix/release-{version}-*` | `release/**` | `release/**`, then forward-merged to `develop` | Treated like `feature/*` | Only path for code-logic fixes on a release | | `hotfix/*` | `main` | `main` + `develop` | **2** (both squad leads) | Urgent prod fixes only, must back-merge to `develop` | | `develop` | — | — | **2** (one owning squad + one cross-squad) | Human commits only; required check `unit-tests`, no bypass, must be up to date | | `main` | — | — | **2** (both squad leads) | Human commits only; same no-bypass rules | - **Mechanical branch lock (not just documented):** `.claude/settings.json` has a `PreToolUse` hook on `Write|Edit|NotebookEdit` that runs `git branch --show-current` and hard-blocks (`exit 1`) any file write if the branch is `develop` or `main`. This is the actual enforcement of AGENTS.md Hard Rule #1 for Claude Code sessions — GitHub branch protection is the enforcement for everyone/everything else. - **`branch-target-guard`** (`protected-file-guard.yml`) hard-blocks (`exit 1`) a PR from a `feature/*` head branch targeting `main` directly. - Release tagging: `scripts/tagRelease.sh v{version}` run from `main` post-merge creates `v{version}` + `release/digital/v{version}` tags; `sprint/{N}/{date}` tags are created automatically by CI (`deploy-dev.yml`'s `tag-sprint` job) when `scripts/sprint.txt` changes. - Direct commits to a `release/**` branch are restricted to no-logic changes (copy fixes, version bumps, flag toggles) and require explicit squad-lead approval (Confluence: Branching Guide, page 304840733). --- ## 2. File Protection Tiers Four-tier system, cross-checked across `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`, `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`, `CODEOWNERS`, and `protected-file-guard.yml` — all three enforcement surfaces agree. | Tier | Examples | Enforcement | |---|---|---| | **Tier 1 — Frozen** | `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`, Tier-1 commerce hooks (`use-current-basket.ts`, `use-current-customer.ts`, `use-navigation.ts`, `use-multi-site.ts`, `use-einstein.ts`, `use-datacloud.ts`, `use-refresh-token.ts`), `config/`, `overrides/app/ssr.js` + `ssr/`, `worker/main.js`, root `package.json`, `mobify.config.js`, `overrides/app/config/countries.ts`, `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`, test/tooling configs (`vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `lighthouserc.js`, `.browserstack.yml`), `.github/workflows/`, governance files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`, `.claude/rules/`, `.claude/settings.json`, `coderabbit.yaml`, `.coderabbit/`, `semgrep.yml`, `scripts/hooks/pre-commit`, `scripts/hooks/commit-msg`) | CODEOWNERS routes to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`; branch protection requires a code-owner approving review before merge (the real, working gate); `tier1-guard` job posts a non-blocking warning + owner map (can't be a hard-fail required check — GitHub disabled cross-run check-run status updates in Feb 2025) | | **Tier 2 — Protected** | Global shell (`header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/`, `seo/`, `_app/`, `_app-config/`, `routes.tsx`), shared product components (`product-tile/`, `product-item/`, `display-price/`, `image-gallery/`, `swatch-group/`, `recommended-products/`), shared commerce components (`order-summary/`, `promo-code/`, `pickup-or-delivery/`), `theme/components/`, `translations/`, 8 named shared hooks (5+ consumers), `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`, `scripts/contentful/sync.js` + `content-types/` | CODEOWNERS routes to owning squad team **+** `@ZimmermannAU/tier-2-approvers` **+** `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` (Tier-1 approvers can also clear Tier 2); `tier2-warning` job posts a non-blocking PR comment listing changed files + reviewer checklist | | **Tier 3 — Squad territory** | e.g. `overrides/app/pages/cart/` → Squad A, `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` → Squad B | CODEOWNERS routes to the owning squad only, no approver gate; `cross-squad-guard` posts a non-blocking comment if a single PR touches both squads' territory | | **Unclassified** | Everything else under `overrides/` | Normal feature-branch workflow | - Required-status-check strings referenced in the Confluence CI/CD setup checklist (305430530): `🔴 Tier 1 — Frozen Files Check`, `🔴 Branch Target Check`, `🟡 Tier 2 — Protected Files Warning`, `🟡 Cross-Squad Boundary Check` — the 🔴 items are hard-fail/required, the 🟡 items are warning-only. - GitHub teams backing CODEOWNERS: `design-system`, `integration-lead`, `squad-a-lead`, `squad-b-lead`, `squad-leads`, `pwa-squad-a`, `pwa-squad-b`, `tier-1-approvers`, `tier-2-approvers`, `pwa-qa-team` (owns `e2e/`). --- ## 3. CI/CD Pipeline (`.github/workflows/`) | Workflow | Trigger | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `qa.yml` | PR → `develop` or `release/**` | Required check. `detect-changes` computes scoped booleans (`storybook`/`e2e`/`vitest`) from changed files since the previous push (not merge-base) via job-level `if:` rather than `on.paths`, so a skipped job still reports "success" instead of leaving the check stuck pending. Jobs: `unit-tests` (Vitest), `storybook-test` (`@storybook/test-runner` + `addon-a11y`), `e2e-localhost` (Playwright chromium + mobile-chrome, 15 min timeout), `e2e-browserstack` (develop-targeted PRs only run if a `SFCC-\d+` Jira key is found in title/body/branch; `release/**` PRs always run the full suite unscoped) | | `protected-file-guard.yml` | PR → `develop`/`main`/`release/**` | `tier1-guard` (warning), `branch-target-guard` (hard block), `tier2-warning` (warning), `cross-squad-guard` (warning) — see §2 | | `digital-sit.yml` ("SIT Gate") | Push/PR → `release/**` | `playwright-p0`, `lighthouse-ci` (`lhci autorun`), `contract-tests` (currently a **stub** — `npm run test:contracts` echoes a TODO and exits 0, not a real assertion yet), `bundle-size` (`npm run test:max-file-size`) → `sit-gate` aggregates all four, `exit 1` on any failure. This is the required check for merging into `release/**`. | | `deploy-dev.yml` | Push → `develop` | `contract-tests` + `bundle-size` gate (`dev-gate`) → `deploy-dev` (`npm run push:dev`) → `tag-sprint` | | `deploy-sit.yml` | `workflow_run` | Only deploys if the upstream SIT Gate workflow concluded `success` | | `deploy-stg.yml` / `deploy-uat.yml` / `deploy-prod.yml` | `workflow_dispatch` only | Manual promotion; `deploy-prod` has **no gate job** — fully manual, relies on the GitHub Environment's required reviewer (see §9) | | `upstream-release-watch.yml` | Weekly cron | Opens a GitHub issue when upstream `pwa-kit`'s release tag differs from the marker in `.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md` | | `weekly-agents.yml` | Weekly cron | `quality-sweep` (components/hooks missing a story or test), `contentful-drift-audit` (orphaned `*ContentfulDefinition.ts` files), `changelog-reminder` | **Digital SIT Gate thresholds:** | Signal | Tool | Threshold | |---|---|---| | Playwright P0 | Playwright | 100% pass, all storefront configs, `retries: 0` (flaky tests must be fixed, not retried away) | | Lighthouse CI | LHCI, 3 runs | Performance ≥80, Accessibility ≥90, Best Practices ≥90; >5pt drop blocks | | Contract tests | Pact/OpenAPI (MuleSoft) | Any schema breach blocks — **currently a non-functional stub**, open dependency owned by Zimmermann integration + Accenture delivery lead | | Bundle size | bundlewatch/bundlesize | `main.js` <180kB, `vendor.js` <250–550kB (see §11 discrepancy), `main.css` <50kB | **Known scoping logic worth knowing:** - Change-scoped E2E only narrows to one area (e.g. `checkout`) if *every* e2e-relevant changed file falls inside that single area's allow-list; anything outside falls back to the full suite by design. - Dependency-change detection diffs only `package.json`'s `dependencies` block (not the lockfile) between pushes to decide whether to force `e2e`/`vitest` on. - `Detect Jira story keys` reads PR title/body/branch into an `env:` var (not directly interpolated into a shell command) specifically to avoid shell injection from attacker-controlled PR text. --- ## 4. AI PR Review Tooling **CodeRabbit (`coderabbit.yaml`)** — `profile: assertive`, `request_changes_workflow: true`. - Per-path `path_instructions`: a repo-wide baseline for `overrides/**` (TS-only, SSR window/document guards, React Query invalidation, Chakra tokens, i18n, multi-region, Einstein/DataCloud events, a11y, perf, no `console.log`, conventional commits), plus escalated instructions for Tier 1/2 paths (`theme/foundation/**`, the named Tier-1 hooks, `config/**`, `mobify.config.js`, `.github/workflows/**`, `ssr.js`, `header/**`, `routes.tsx`, `product-tile/**`, `display-price/**`, checkout/PDP/PLP pages, `e2e/features/**`). - Tools enabled: `eslint`, `gitleaks` (secret detection), `ast-grep` (→ `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`), `osvScanner` (OSV.dev dependency vuln scan), `reactDoctor`, `semgrep` (→ `semgrep.yml`). - `pre_merge_checks`: `title`/`description` = **error** mode (conventional-commit format), `issue_assessment` = warning (Jira Forge app not yet installed), custom **`Docstring convention compliance`** check = **error** mode (JSDoc required on shared components/exported hooks/non-obvious utils). - `path_filters` excludes derived config files from review entirely (`.cursor/rules/**`, `.vscode/instructions/**`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.claude/registry/*.md`, `package-lock.json`). **`.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`** (mechanically enforces the a11y rules in `.claude/rules/components.md`): - `img-missing-alt.yml` — `` without `alt` - `icon-button-missing-aria-label.yml` — `IconButton*` without `aria-label` - `clickable-non-interactive-element.yml` — `div|span|Box|Flex|Stack|VStack|HStack|Grid|Text|PopoverFooter|PopoverHeader` with `onClick` but no `role` - `utils/jsx-element.yml` — shared matcher used by the three rules above **`semgrep.yml`** (2 rules): - `payment-credential-logged` (ERROR, taint mode) — sources match `(?i)(cardNumber|cvv|pin|cardNum|pan)`; sinks are `console.$METHOD(...)` / `Sentry.$METHOD(...)` - `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` (ERROR) — flags `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html: $X}}` unless `$X` is wrapped in `$SANITIZER.sanitize(...)` Both files are Tier 1 — weakening a rule here removes a check with no signal in `coderabbit.yaml` itself, which is why they're locked down alongside it. --- ## 5. Git Hooks (Husky v9) Wired via `.husky/pre-commit` / `.husky/commit-msg` (thin wrappers delegating to `scripts/hooks/`), auto-installed by the `"prepare": "husky"` script on `npm install`. Manual fallback documented in `scripts/hooks/README.md`. **`pre-commit`** (blocking, `exit 1`, unless noted): 1. Regenerates `.claude/registry/` when staged files touch `overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages}/` or `routes.tsx`; auto-stages the result. 2. Regenerates `.cursor/rules/`, `.vscode/instructions/`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` via `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix` when a `.claude/rules/*.md` or skill file is staged; **non-blocking** warning if a skill changed and `.claude/skills/README.md`/the mirrored Confluence page wasn't also updated. 3. Contentful Studio Experiences codegen — regenerates `definitions.ts` from staged `experiences/*.tsx`; **blocks** on codegen failure. 4. **Derived-config guard** — blocks any modified `.cursor/rules/*`, `.vscode/instructions/*`, or `.github/copilot-instructions.md` whose `synced-from:` source file isn't staged in the same commit (prevents drift between AI tool configs). 5. **`.env.sample` secret guard** — blocks if any `_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET`-suffixed key has a non-empty value, or any value looks like a JWT, 32+ char hex, 40+ char base64, or a known provider-token prefix (`AKIA...`, `ghp_...`, `ghs_...`, `sk-...`, `xox[bpars]-...`). **`commit-msg`** — enforces conventional commits: `^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync)(\([a-z0-9/._-]+\))?: .{1,100}$`, exempting `Merge`/`Revert`/`fixup!`/`squash!`/`WIP`; blocks with a usage message on mismatch. --- ## 6. Claude Code Session Harness (`.claude/settings.json`) - **`PreToolUse`** on `Write|Edit|NotebookEdit`: branch-lock check (see §1) + runs `.claude/hooks/tier2Warn.sh` if present. - **`PostToolUse`**: Prettier auto-run on new `Write`s; `.claude/hooks/contentfulDriftWarn.sh` (⚠️ referenced but not found on disk — dangling hook reference, see §11) and `.claude/hooks/registryUpdate.sh` on `Edit|Write`; `.claude/hooks/testFileRemind.sh` on `Write`. - **`Stop`**: `.claude/hooks/session-reflect.sh` — if anything changed this session, returns a `block` decision forcing Claude to write a proposal file to `.docs/agents-proposals/-.md` suggesting doc updates, rather than editing governance docs directly itself. Has a re-entry guard to avoid looping. - **`permissions.allow`** pre-approves read-only/low-risk Bash (`git branch/status/diff/log/show`, `find`, `grep`, `ls`, `npm run lint/test/build`, `gh pr/api/issue`) so routine reads don't prompt. - Client-side hook scripts in `.claude/hooks/` are all **non-blocking** (`exit 0` always): `tier2Warn.sh` (path-matches Tier 2 groups, prints owner/notify warning), `registryUpdate.sh` (incremental `.claude/registry/` regen), `testFileRemind.sh` (reminds, doesn't block, on missing co-located test file). - **Pre-flight skills** that gate *before* Claude acts: `/scope-check` (classifies every file a proposed prompt would touch by tier, verdicts SAFE/RISKY/BLOCKED, rewrites unsafe prompts), `/audit-tier` (tier/owner/blast-radius lookup for a single file). --- ## 7. TypeScript / Lint / Build Enforcement - **`tsconfig.json`**: `strict: true`, `noEmit: true`, `isolatedModules: true`, `skipLibCheck: true`; path aliases `~/*` → `./*`, `app/*` → `./overrides/app/*`. - **`.eslintrc.js`**: extends `@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/eslint`; TS-specific rules (`no-floating-promises`, `no-inferrable-types`, `restrict-template-expressions`, `no-misused-promises`, `require-await`) are all set to `warn`, not `error`. **Confirms AGENTS.md's own claim**: no `max-lines-per-function` or `complexity` rule is configured — the ~150-line/complexity guidance in `.claude/rules/components.md` is a self-check, not an ESLint-enforced gate, today. - **`babel.config.js`**: extends `@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/babel/babel-config` + `babel-plugin-module-resolver` for the same aliases — part of the path-alias sync group (see §11). - Path-alias sync group is actually **5 files**, not 4 as AGENTS.md states: `babel.config.js`, `tsconfig.json`, `.storybook/main.js`, `vitest.config.ts`, and `jest.config.js` (the last for `pwa-kit-dev` internals only — see §11). --- ## 8. Test Harness | Layer | Config | Key settings | |---|---|---| | Vitest | `vitest.config.ts` + `vitest.setup.ts` | `environment: 'jsdom'`, `include: overrides/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`, `passWithNoTests: true`; no coverage-threshold config | | Storybook | `.storybook/main.js` + `preview.tsx` | `addon-a11y` enabled; `a11y.test: 'error'` — **a11y violations fail** `test-storybook --ci` runs | | Playwright | `playwright.config.js` | `retries: 2` (CI only, `0` for the `p0` project), `workers: 1`; projects: `p0` (SIT gate), `chromium`/`mobile-chrome`, `a11y-mobile`/`a11y-desktop`, `extra-features-*` | | BrowserStack | `.browserstack.yml` | `testSuite: e2e/tests/zimm` only (scope locked — a wider scope means CI cost explosion); Chrome/Safari/Firefox/Edge across macOS Sonoma + Windows 11; `testObservability: true` synced to Zephyr | | Lighthouse | `lighthouserc.js` | 3 runs; `performance ≥0.80`, `accessibility ≥0.90`, `best-practices ≥0.90`, all error-level | All five config surfaces are Tier 1 (`frozenFiles.md`) — a change here breaks every contributor's harness, so they route to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`. --- ## 9. Environment, Secrets & Deployment Gates - **`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`** (`npm run env`): `init` scaffolds env files from GitHub Environments; `validate [--live]` cross-checks scope placement and can make live read-only Contentful/SLAS calls; **`push ` is gated to tier-1-approvers only** via a live `gh api` identity + team-membership check; `scope:personal` keys are excluded from any centralized push/pull. - **`.env.sample`** scope tagging (`# scope:shared|tier|personal|auto`, own comment line, never trailing) exists specifically so a blank placeholder doesn't read as non-empty to the pre-commit secret guard. - **GitHub Environments** (per Confluence 304840708 — Environment Topology & Promotion Path): `staging` (no reviewer), `sit`/`pre-prod` (Zimmermann environment owner reviewer), `uat` (Zimmermann stakeholder reviewer), `production` (release-manager manual approval reviewer). SIT secrets are explicitly not accessible to the `production` workflow. - **Promotion path gates**: DEV requires the Digital SIT Gate; STAGE requires Digital SIT Gate green **and** manual NewStore OMS SIT sign-off; UAT requires per-region business stakeholder sign-off; PROD requires release-manager approval **plus** an AU canary (<0.5% error rate over 2h) before wider rollout. - **SIT-specific rules** (Confluence 285540356): manual SIT deploys must use `sit/*` or `hotfix/*`; never push to SIT without Digital Dev green; never enable Einstein/Global-e/Narvar on SIT; SIT is never a hotfix path to PROD (`hotfix/* → main → PROD` only); a broken SIT does not block the Digital release train. --- ## 10. Contentful Sync Safety - **`scripts/contentful/sync.js`** is confirmed additive-only in the actual code: field merging explicitly preserves any existing field not in the local definition (`ct.fields = [...(ct.fields ?? []).filter(f => !defIds.has(f.id)), ...fields]`) — it can never delete a field from a live content type. - Approval-gated npm scripts (Confluence 318472193): `setup:contentful` and `promote:alias` require a **Tier 1 approver**; `config:contentful` (writes) also Tier 1 approver-only, read-only view open to any dev; `sync:contentful` and `detect:drift` open to any developer. - `detectDrift` runs automatically before migrations apply (bypassable with `--force`) and doubles as a CI-usable gate (`npm run detect:drift` exits non-zero on drift). - Contentful environment roles restrict content-type editing on `sit`/`staging`/`uat`/`master` to the CI service account only — human editors get entry/asset CRUD there but can't touch content types. --- ## 11. AI-Assisted QA — Six-Stage Pipeline (Confluence) Three explicit **human gates** in an otherwise Claude/agent-assisted pipeline (per 277807105: *"No AC is approved without BA sign-off. No test case is created without Tester review. No PR is merged without human code review."*): | Stage | What happens | Gate | |---|---|---| | 1. Story Intake | BA structures the Jira story to a fixed template | none (garbage-in/garbage-out risk) | | 2. AC Authoring with Claude | Claude drafts acceptance criteria | **Human Gate 1** — BA reviews every line, sets Jira status "AC Approved" | | 3. Zephyr Test Case Creation (MCP) | Claude drafts test cases | **Human Gate 2** — Tester reviews and marks "Ready for Execution" before anything is created in Zephyr | | 4. Branch & governance (who can change what) 6 7 - **GitFlow branch rules** (AGENTS.md, [Branching Guide](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/304840733)): `feature/*`/`fix/*` from `develop`; `release/**` supervised (plan-first, confirm-every-edit, code fixes only via `fix/release-*` sub-branches); `hotfix/*` from `main`, back-merged to `develop`; `develop`/`main` are human-commit-only and Claude is **physically blocked** from writing to them via a branch-lock hook in `.claude/settings.json`. 8 - **3-tier file protection**: Tier 1 (`.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` — design tokens, commerce SDK hooks, runtime config, build pipeline, CI/CD, governance files) needs named-owner approval; Tier 2 (`.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` — shared components/hooks, translations, theme components) needs a second reviewer; Tier 3 is plain squad ownership. 9 - **CODEOWNERS** routes every Tier 1/2 path to real GitHub teams (`tier-1-approvers`, `tier-2-approvers`, squad teams); enforced by required code-owner review in branch protection — the actual gate, not Claude's own confirmation prompts. 10 - **Branch protection**: `develop` requires 2 approvals + `unit-tests` status check; `main` requires 2 approvals (both squad leads); `release/**` requires the composite `Digital SIT Gate` check, no admin bypass. 11 - **`.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml`**: `tier1-guard`/`tier2-guard` post warnings/owner-contact maps (non-blocking by design); `branch-target-guard` hard-blocks `feature/*` → `main`; `cross-squad-guard` warns when a PR spans both squads' domains. 12 13 ## 2. Security 14 15 - **Secrets**: never committed — real values in gitignored `.env.`/`.env.shared`, injected as MRT env vars on deploy. `.env.sample` is template-only (names, no values). `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` blocks a commit if a secret-class key (`*_TOKEN`, `*_API_KEY`, `*_DSN`, etc.) has a non-empty value or matches a known credential pattern (JWT, AWS `AKIA…`, GitHub `ghp_`, Slack `xox…`). 16 - **Payment credentials**: never logged/persisted client-side, submitted only in POST bodies, masked after submit (`.claude/rules/conventions.md`) — enforced by the `payment-credential-logged` semgrep rule. 17 - **XSS**: `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` must wrap a sanitizer call — enforced by the `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` semgrep rule. 18 - **CodeRabbit** (`coderabbit.yaml`) additionally wires in `gitleaks` (secret scanning), `osvScanner` (dependency CVEs), `eslint`, `reactDoctor`, and ast-grep — all as advisory PR-review signal, not a merge gate. 19 - **Env-var security boundary table** ([TSD §4.1](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585)): every integration credential is classified browser-direct (public) vs MRT-mediated (server-only) vs CI-only — e.g. Contentful Preview/Management tokens, MuleSoft/Booxi/GiveX credentials, and reCAPTCHA secret key never reach the browser bundle. 20 - **Blast-radius containment** (same TSD §12.1): per-upstream SSR connection pools so a flooded integration (e.g. checkout) can't starve unrelated ones (Contentful, SLAS JWKS). 21 - **Consent fails closed**: unknown consent state → no third-party script loads at all (Didomi). 22 23 ## 3. Development process 24 25 - Four-step workflow enforced by AGENTS.md: clarify → plan → copy-first (base template files copied to `overrides/` with a marker `console.log` before functional changes) → implement, with an optional local CodeRabbit pass before commit. 26 - TypeScript-only inside `overrides/`, strict mode; no `any` without a comment; DRY/KISS/SOLID; no magic numbers; Australian spelling for Zimmermann code. 27 - **No mocking in production paths** — all data from live Commerce Cloud API. 28 - **Minimal-changes rule**: no upward refactors, no renaming shared hooks/components, no silent scope creep. 29 - Git hooks: `commit-msg` enforces Conventional Commits; `pre-commit` also regenerates derived AI-config files and Contentful `definitions.ts`, and blocks hand-edits to derived config files bypassing their source. 30 31 ## 4. Delivery / CI-CD gates 32 33 - **`qa.yml`** (every PR to `develop`/`release/**`): unit tests always run; Storybook interaction + a11y and Playwright are path-scoped to the diff (change-scoped E2E); BrowserStack cross-browser only runs when a Jira key is detected in the PR (develop) or unscoped on `release/**`. 34 - **`digital-sit.yml` / Digital SIT Gate** (required check on `release/**`): Playwright P0 (100% pass, 0 retries — flaky tests must be fixed not retried), Lighthouse CI (Perf ≥80, A11y ≥90, Best Practices ≥90, no >5pt regression), MuleSoft contract tests (currently a **placeholder**, exits 0 — open dependency pending MuleSoft OpenAPI spec), bundle size (`main.js`<180kB, `vendor.js`<250kB, `main.css`<50kB via bundlewatch). 35 - **Deploy workflows**: `deploy-dev` auto on push to `develop` (gated on contract-tests+bundle-size); `deploy-sit` auto after SIT Gate passes; `deploy-uat`/`deploy-stg`/`deploy-prod` are all manual `workflow_dispatch` only, each behind its own GitHub `environment:` (reviewer protection configured at repo-settings level). 36 - **STAGE promotion** is a manual, non-automated checklist: SIT Gate green + NewStore SIT complete + Integration Lead/squad-lead sign-off. 37 - Weekly automation: `upstream-release-watch.yml` flags new `@salesforce/retail-react-app` releases; `weekly-agents.yml` flags missing tests/stories, Contentful drift, and changelog gaps. 38 39 ## 5. Testing / QA 40 41 - 3 layers, no duplicated coverage: Vitest (logic), Storybook `play` (interaction), Playwright (E2E) — see `.claude/rules/testing.md`. 42 - **Gherkin-first workflow**: `.feature` file → Lead QA sign-off in plain English → Playwright spec generated only after approval. 43 - **Multi-region fixtures** from day one (7 storefronts × 11 locales) — no hardcoded region. 44 - **AI-Assisted QA six-stage pipeline** ([overview](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/277544962)) with three mandatory human gates: BA approves AC (Gate 1), Tester approves Zephyr cases (Gate 2), Developer reviews any agent-raised fix PR (Gate 3) — the triage agent never touches Tier 1 files, always raises a Jira defect instead. 45 46 ## 6. Accessibility 47 48 - Target WCAG 2.2 AA (2.1 AA floor). Mechanically enforced via `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`: missing ``, missing `IconButton aria-label`, clickable non-interactive elements missing `role`. Plus `vitest-axe`, `axe-playwright`, Storybook a11y addon, and the Lighthouse A11y ≥90 CI threshold. 49 50 ## 7. Performance 51 52 - LCP ≤2s p75 mobile is the binding constraint. All Didomi-gated third-party scripts must defer/async/post-hydration load (documented exception: Optimizely Web loads pre-render to avoid flicker, US-only). Bundle-size ceilings enforced in CI (above). 53 54 ## 8. Consent, privacy & graceful degradation 55 56 - Didomi gates every third-party script, fails closed on unknown consent. Marketing opt-in unchecked by default except US (pre-checked); syncs FE→SFCC→Omneo→Emarsys, retries silently, never blocks checkout. GDPR (DSAR/erasure) handled by the SFCC cartridge. Each external integration has a documented failure mode (§12 of the TSD) — e.g. Global-e failure surfaces an explicit error rather than silently falling back to SFCC checkout; Omneo reads are load-bearing for My Account and must show explicit retry UI rather than partial data. 57 58 ## 9. Release & dependency policy 59 60 - Supervised editing on `release/*`/`hotfix/*` per `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`; GitFlow back-merges mandatory to keep `develop` aligned. 61 - Upstream `@salesforce/retail-react-app` bumps are opportunistic (security/CVE or a wanted fix), never scheduled, per `.docs/upstreamPolicy.md`. 62 63 ## Known gaps / exceptions worth knowing about 64 65 - The SIT gate's MuleSoft contract-test check is a no-op placeholder. 66 - reCAPTCHA provides no bot protection in EU/UK for consent-declining visitors (accepted tradeoff). 67 - GitHub Environment Variables (used for centralized shared/tier config) are plaintext-readable by collaborators — a deliberate, documented exception to the secrets policy, gated to `tier-1-approvers` only. 68 - Per an earlier Confluence read, the "Development Standards" and "Component Override Strategy" pages still describe a `custom/` sub-folder for new components and a direct-import icon pattern that both contradict current AGENTS.md/repo convention — worth flagging to whoever owns those pages. 69

input.content: # Zimmermann PWA Kit — Software Engineering Harnesses & Guardrails _Compiled from a full sweep of the `zimmermann-pwa` repo and the Confluence `SFCC` space, 2026-07-16._ _Scope: mechanisms that automatically enforce quality, security, or process — not general conventions that rely on a human/Claude reading a doc._ --- ## 1. Security & Privacy Boundaries (Confluence — Technical Solution Design, 256835585) **Consent gate (Didomi):** fail-closed — if consent state can't be determined, **no third-party script loads at all**. Everything from GTM/Addingwell, Inside Chat, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Narvar Promise, Measmerize, Vimeo, and Recently Viewed must gate on a Didomi purpose ID (several purpose IDs are still an open item pending provisioning; the one documented exception is reCAPTCHA v3, which needs no consent outside EU/UK and loads only on form interaction). Marketing opt-in is unchecked by default on all storefronts except US (pre-checked), and syncs FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys. **Credential boundary (by integration):** SLAS client ID is the only browser-direct SFCC credential; Google Maps, Contentful Preview/Management, MuleSoft/Booxi are MRT-mediated only; Adyen/Narvar/Global-e/GTM/Didomi/reCAPTCHA site-key are public-by-design browser-direct values, with their paired secret (API key/HMAC/secret key) always MRT-mediated. Contentful Management tokens are CI-only, never deployed to MRT. **SSR vs CSR boundary:** PDP/PLP/content/home/boutique = full SSR (SEO/LCP-critical). Cart/checkout/My Account/order history/wishlist/address book = SSR shell + CSR data (personalised, behind auth, blocked in `robots.txt`, and SSR-rendering personalised data risks state leaking across requests under load). **Blast-radius containment:** each upstream origin (SFCC SCAPI/SLAS JWKS, SFCC Payments, MuleSoft, Google Places, Booxi) gets its own SSR `undici` connection pool with an independent concurrency cap, so a slow/flooded integration (e.g. checkout) can't starve unrelated origins. GiveX balance calls are explicitly flagged as carrying payment credentials and must never queue behind other traffic. **Graceful degradation:** each external integration fails independently and has a documented failure mode (TSD §12) — e.g. a Global-e outage must surface an explicit error rather than silently falling back to SFCC checkout; Omneo reads are load-bearing for My Account and must show explicit retry UI rather than partial/stale data. --- ## 13. Contentful Sync Safety - **`scripts/contentful/sync.js`** is confirmed additive-only in the actual code: field merging explicitly preserves any existing field not in the local definition (`ct.fields = [...(ct.fields ?? []).filter(f => !defIds.has(f.id)), ...fields]`) — it can never delete a field from a live content type. - Approval-gated npm scripts (Confluence 318472193): `setup:contentful` and `promote:alias` require a **Tier 1 approver**; `config:contentful` (writes) also Tier 1 approver-only, read-only view open to any dev; `sync:contentful` and `detect:drift` open to any developer. - `detectDrift` runs automatically before migrations apply (bypassable with `--force`) and doubles as a CI-usable gate (`npm run detect:drift` exits non-zero on drift). - Contentful environment roles restrict content-type editing on `sit`/`staging`/`uat`/`master` to the CI service account only — human editors get entry/asset CRUD there but can't touch content types. --- ## 11. AI-Assisted QA — Six-Stage Pipeline (Confluence) Three explicit **human gates** in an otherwise Claude/agent-assisted pipeline (per 277807105: *"No AC is approved without BA sign-off. No test case is created without Tester review. No PR is merged without human code review."*): | Stage | What happens | Gate | |---|---|---| | 1. Story Intake | BA structures the Jira story to a fixed template | none (garbage-in/garbage-out risk) | | 2. AC Authoring with Claude | Claude drafts acceptance criteria | **Human Gate 1** — BA reviews every line, sets Jira status "AC Approved" | | 3. Zephyr Test Case Creation (MCP) | Claude drafts test cases | **Human Gate 2** — Tester reviews and marks "Ready for Execution" before anything is created in Zephyr | | 4. Playwright Spec Authoring | Developer fills in real selectors, confirms local pass | Manual step, no formal gate | | 5. BrowserStack Execution | 7 storefronts × 4 browsers, results auto-sync to Zephyr | Runs on PR to `release/**` | | 6. Defect Triage & Fix Branch | Agent classifies failures by tier, acts within tier limits | **Human Gate 3** — no PR is ever merged without human code review | **AI-Assisted Defect Triage Agent guardrails** (Confluence 277708843, most detailed automated-agent doc found): - No auto-merge, ever — branch protection on `develop`/`release/**` can't be bypassed by any workflow or bot. - Tier 1 hard stop is enforced **deterministically** by `classify-tier.js` (a CODEOWNERS lookup) — never delegated to the LLM's judgment. - Tier 2 auto-fix is permitted, but the PR carries a `tier-2-change` label and a CODEOWNERS-enforced second reviewer. - Credentials are never placed in LLM prompt context. - Agent PRs carry an `agent-raised` label and a `fix/agent-` branch prefix; CodeRabbit reviews them identically to human PRs. - Jira writes go through a scoped service-account token (issue create/link only — no admin/bulk/cross-project). - Runs on **AWS Bedrock** (Haiku for classification, Sonnet for investigation/fix) rather than the Anthropic API directly, since the Atlassian MCP integration can't run on a GitHub Actions runner. **Programme-wide Agent Registry constraints** (Confluence 278921217) apply to *every* AI agent in the project, not just this one: Bedrock-only for automated/CI contexts, deterministic Tier-1 stop, no auto-merge ever, human gate on all code changes, MCP for interactive writes vs REST API for CI writes, credentials in CI secrets only. A CodeRabbit check also flags any new agent file that isn't matched by a registry update. --- ## 12. Security & Privacy Boundaries (Confluence — Technical Solution Design, 256835585) **Consent gate (Didomi):** fail-closed — if consent state can't be determined, **no third-party script loads at all**. Everything from GTM/Addingwell, Inside Chat, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Narvar Promise, Measmerize, Vimeo, and Recently Viewed must gate on a Didomi purpose ID (several purpose IDs are still an open item pending provisioning; the one documented exception is reCAPTCHA v3, which needs no consent outside EU/UK and loads only on form interaction). Marketing opt-in is unchecked by default on all storefronts except US (pre-checked), and syncs FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys. **Credential boundary (by integration):** SLAS client ID is the only browser-direct SFCC credential; Google Maps, Contentful Preview/Management, MuleSoft/Booxi are MRT-mediated only; Adyen/Narvar/Global-e/GTM/Didomi/reCAPTCHA site-key are public-by-design browser-direct values, with their paired secret (API key/HMAC/secret key) always MRT-mediated. Contentful Management tokens are CI-only, never deployed to MRT. **SSR vs CSR boundary:** PDP/PLP/content/home/boutique = full SSR (SEO/LCP-critical). Cart/checkout/My Account/order history/wishlist/address book = SSR shell + CSR data (personalised, behind auth, blocked in `robots.txt`, and SSR-rendering personalised data risks state leaking across requests under load). **Blast-radius containment:** each upstream origin (SFCC SCAPI/SLAS JWKS, SFCC Payments, MuleSoft, Google Places, Booxi) gets its own SSR `undici` connection pool with an independent concurrency cap, so a slow/flooded integration (e.g. checkout) can't starve unrelated origins. GiveX balance calls are explicitly flagged as carrying payment credentials and must never queue behind other traffic. **Graceful degradation:** each external integration fails independently and has a documented failure mode (TSD §12) — e.g. a Global-e outage must surface an explicit error rather than silently falling back to SFCC checkout; Omneo reads are load-bearing for My Account and must show explicit retry UI rather than partial/stale data. --- ## 13. Known Gaps & Drift Worth Flagging These surfaced during the sweep and are not yet resolved — flagging per AGENTS.md's doc-integrity rule rather than silently ignoring them: - **`test:contracts` is a non-functional stub** — `npm run test:contracts` always exits 0 with a TODO; the "Contract tests" signal in the Digital SIT Gate is not a real assertion yet. Open dependency owned by the Zimmermann integration team + Accenture delivery lead. - **`tests/lighthouserc.js` path drift** — `package.json`'s `test:lighthouse` script and both `frozenFiles.md`/CODEOWNERS reference a `tests/lighthouserc.js` path that doesn't exist on disk; only the root `lighthouserc.js` exists and is what `digital-sit.yml` actually runs (implicit default resolution, no `--config` flag). Latent, not currently broken, but worth a docs/script cleanup. - **Dangling hook reference** — `.claude/settings.json`'s `PostToolUse` config references `.claude/hooks/contentfulDriftWarn.sh`, which doesn't exist on disk. - **Path-alias sync group is 5 files, not 4** — `.docs/architecture.md` names `babel.config.js`, `tsconfig.json`, `.storybook/main.js`, `vitest.config.ts`, **and** `jest.config.js`; AGENTS.md's frozenFiles note only lists 4 (omits `jest.config.js`, which serves `pwa-kit-dev` internals only). - **No Renovate/Dependabot bot configured** — despite `coderabbit.yaml` anticipating dependency-bump PR titles (`chore(deps)`), no bot actually opens them; `osvScanner` (via CodeRabbit) is the only automated dependency-vulnerability signal today. - **reCAPTCHA provides no bot protection in EU/UK for consent-declining visitors** — an accepted tradeoff of the fail-closed consent policy, not a bug. - **Confluence vs. repo conflicts** (pre-existing, from a 2026-07-15 audit): Confluence's "Development Standards"/"Component Override Strategy" pages still say to import icons from `@salesforce/retail-react-app` directly (repo says the opposite — always `overrides/app/components/icons`) and to put new components under a `custom/` subfolder (repo convention has no `custom/` layer). "Technical Environment Setup" (304906242) still describes a flat `.env` copy with no mention of the tiered `.env.shared`/`.env.` system. Trust the repo over Confluence where they disagree; these pages need an update. - **Locale count discrepancy** (pre-existing, from the same audit): AGENTS.md/testing.md state "11 active locales" across 8 storefronts; both Confluence locale tables (Contentful Ops page + Product TSD) agree on 9 unique locale codes for the same 8 storefronts. Not yet resolved or raised with the user. --- ## Sources **Repo:** `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/*.md`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/hooks/*`, `.claude/skills/scope-check`, `.claude/skills/audit-tier`, `CODEOWNERS`, `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, `coderabbit.yaml`, `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/*`, `semgrep.yml`, `scripts/hooks/pre-commit`, `scripts/hooks/commit-msg`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`, `scripts/contentful/sync.js`, `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs`, `tsconfig.json`, `.eslintrc.js`, `babel.config.js`, `package.json`, `vitest.config.ts`, `playwright.config.js`, `.storybook/*`, `.browserstack.yml`, `lighthouserc.js`, `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, `.docs/architecture.md`, `.docs/upstreamPolicy.md`, `.docs/memory/*`. **Confluence (space `SFCC`):** 304840733 (Branching Guide), 305561601 (CI/CD Pipeline), 304840754 (SIT Quality Gates), 277544962 + 277577757/277708807/277676053/305528833 (AI-Assisted QA pipeline), 261750785/261881857 (Development Standards / Component Override Strategy), 259358732/259686402/268337165/305430530 (Platform & Tool Access family), 256835585 (Technical Solution Design – PWA), 277708843 (AI-Assisted Defect Triage Agent TSD), 305102849 (Human-in-the-Lead AI Development overview), 304840708 (Environment Topology & Promotion Path), 278921217 (Agent Registry), 285540356 (Environment Details — SIT), 318472193 (Contentful CMS Setup & Operations), 264896514 (SFCC Build/Deployment — Headless), 277807105 (QA & Testing index).
